stem:
The diagram shows Karan's square card of side $8\,\mathrm{cm}$ with centre marked $O$. He wants a circular hole of radius $2\,\mathrm{cm}$ at that centre, drawn with a compass.

Which claim correctly states where the compass point must sit and what radius to use?

options.text: Place the compass point at $O$ and set the radius to $2\,\mathrm{cm}$.
Place the compass point anywhere on the card; only the $2\,\mathrm{cm}$ opening matters.
Place the compass point on the dashed circle and set the radius from there to $O$.
Draw the hole freehand, because neat artwork on the square card is enough.

teacher.key_rationale: The hole needs the tip at centre O with radius 2 cm. Ignoring the centre omits a required condition. Putting the tip on the rim and measuring back to O reverses centre and radius roles. Freehand neatness is outside the compass decision.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as a square card with centre O, dashed circle radius 2 cm, and radius mark; stem refers to the diagram.
